title: After the Colour
source: Midnight Bet — Integrated ARC I — Old Friends, New Heat
paragraphs: Holi cleanup ended. Holi did not. Colour stayed in hair. Under nails. On collars. In memory. By evening, everyone had showered. The body remembered before the skin forgot. Mira sat at home drying her hair. The soft towel against her bare shoulders. The faint remaining pink under her nails. The memory of Aarav’s thumb on her cheek, the way his eyes had stayed on her when the white kurta became translucent with water.

A message from Aarav. Later? She stared. Rooftop. Then cleanup. Then her own word: Later. She typed: Maybe. Deleted. Typed: 9. Rooftop café. Sent. Across town, Aarav smiled. Ananya’s name appeared next. Tomorrow 11. Extra session if you want. He stared at both chats. Two women. Two very different forms of attention. One who asked for honesty and then obeyed when told to look. One who commanded him to remove his jacket and then watched.

He replied Ananya: Yes. Then Mira: See you. Kabir’s phone was worse. Rhea: Home. Meera: Umbrella still with you. Tara: You left pink colour packet in our bag. Three women. Three different histories. Kabir laughed to himself. Then stopped. Nothing about this was simple anymore. The memory of Rhea’s mouth against his in the parking basement. The soft press of Tara’s body when she reached past him. The quiet authority in Meera’s voice when she handed him the umbrella.

Dev had Shalini: Good work today. And Naina: You stared at her. Dev answered Naina first. You stared at Mehul. Naina: Correct. Dev smiled. Then Shalini: Thanks. Shalini typing. Stopped. Typing again. You looked different outside class. Dev’s pulse changed. He replied: So did you. No response for five minutes. Then: See you Tuesday. That was enough. The knowledge that she had noticed him — that the white top and the outdoor light had changed something in her as well — sat under his skin like heat.

At 8:45, Rhea sat at Neha’s kitchen counter. Arjun cooked. Neha showered. Rhea had come to return wedding papers. Bad decision. Arjun did not look at her. That was more noticeable than if he had. Rhea said: “You said something.” Arjun kept cutting vegetables. “I say many things.”

“Not here.” He stopped. Knife down. Looked at her. “Rhea.” She waited. He exhaled. “I am married to your sister.” “I know.” “You are family.” “By marriage.” Arjun’s jaw tightened. The clarification mattered. Rhea continued: “I did not ask you to do anything.”

“No.” “You told me you think about it.” “Yes.” “Why?” Arjun looked toward the hallway. Then her. “Because you keep asking questions I should not answer.” Rhea smiled faintly. “That is not why.” He stepped closer. Not touching. But close enough that she could feel the heat of his body and smell the faint scent of his cologne.

“You want the answer?” “Yes.” “You know you are attractive.” Rhea’s breath shifted. Heat settled low in her stomach. “You know I notice.” “Yes.” “You enjoy making me notice.” Rhea did not deny it. Arjun continued: “And I enjoy that you know.” Silence. No touch. Footsteps. Both stepped apart before Neha entered. Neha looked between them.

“What?” Arjun picked up the knife. “Rhea hates coriander.” Rhea laughed. “True.” Normal dinner. Erotic lie underneath. At Rohan and Tara’s apartment, Kabir arrived with the pink packet. Rohan was on a work call in the bedroom. Tara opened the door. Fresh clothes — a soft top that sat close to her body, damp hair falling over one shoulder, the faint scent of soap still on her skin. Kabir noticed. Tara noticed.

“You came for colour?” “You texted.” “I could have kept it.” “Then why text?” She smiled. Good question. Kabir entered. Tara placed the packet on the table. Neither reached. She said: “Earlier.” Kabir’s pulse changed. “What?” “You said you stepped back because you wanted to step forward.” Kabir looked toward the bedroom. Rohan’s voice muffled behind the door. Tara followed his gaze.

“Yes.” “Exactly.” Kabir whispered: “This is stupid.” “Probably.” “Dangerous.” “Definitely.” He looked at her. “Do you want me to stop coming here?” Tara’s face changed. “No.” Fast. Too fast. Kabir noticed. “So.” Tara crossed her arms. The movement pulled the soft top tighter across her breasts for a second.

“So nothing.” They stood close enough that the air felt occupied. Kabir’s hand lifted. Stopped. Tara looked at it. Then at him. “Not tonight.” Kabir nodded. “Okay.” No sulk. No persuasion. Tara’s expression softened. “Good.” Rohan emerged. Kabir picked up the colour packet.

“Found it.” Rohan laughed. “You came back for twenty rupees colour?” Kabir smiled. “Sentimental.” Tara looked away. The word hung between them like a secret. At 9 p.m., Mira met Aarav at the rooftop café. Not private. Half full. Safer. Maybe. She wore a loose black top that still sat close enough to her body that the soft shape of her breasts was clear when she moved. Aarav wore the same stupid grey jacket. Mira stared at it.

“Remove.” He blinked. “What?” “Nothing.” She laughed. Ananya’s voice had leaked into her imagination — the command, the obedience, the way Aarav had looked at his tutor when told to take the jacket off. Aarav noticed. “Why are you smiling?” “Teacher.” His expression changed.

“Ananya?” Mira nodded. “You listen to her.” “Yes.” “Easily.” “Yes.” Mira leaned forward. “Does she know you kissed me?” Aarav went still. “No.” “Would she care?” He looked at her. “I do not know.” Mira smiled. “Interesting.” The table between them felt smaller than it was. Aarav’s eyes dropped once to the open neckline of her top, to the soft shadow between her breasts, then returned to her face. Mira caught it.

“You are looking.” “Yes.” “Why?” He answered honestly. “Because I remember how you felt against me.” Mira’s pulse jumped. The rooftop. His hands at her waist. The soft give of her body when she kissed him back. She did not look away. “Later,” she had said. Tonight was later. Neither of them moved first. But the heat between them was no longer possible to pretend was anything else. Aarav asked:

“Kiss?” Mira looked around. Public. Not too public. “Outside.” They went to a side terrace. Still visible from glass. No hiding fully. Aarav stopped. “Still?” Mira nodded. “Yes.” He kissed her. Slow. No panic this time. Mira’s hand at his chest. Aarav’s at her waist. They stopped themselves. Not footsteps. Choice. Mira smiled.

“Better.” Aarav: “Much.” She stepped away first. No sex. The heat grew because they stopped. At 9:40, Sana and Mehul had their own conversation. Home. Colour traces still behind Mehul’s ear. Sana pointed. “You missed.” He leaned down. “Fix?” Sana wiped it with wet cloth. Then looked at him.

“You liked Mira.” Mehul did not lie. “Yes.” Sana nodded. “You liked Aarav.” She smiled. “Yes.” Mehul sat. “Problem?” Sana thought. “Not yet.” “Interesting?” “Yes.” They looked at each other. Marriage did not disappear. Neither pretended monogamy questions were easy. Sana said:
“We are not opening anything because Holi was hot.” Mehul laughed. “Agreed.” “But we also are not pretending we did not notice.” “Agreed.” They kissed. Their own kiss. Marriage still present.

Outside desire did not automatically replace it. That complexity would matter later. At 10, Naina and Dev met Sana at the rooftop because lights still needed removing. Sana left after ten minutes. Dev and Naina remained. No rain. Same balcony from before. Naina leaned against railing. “Shalini texted.” Dev looked. “How?”

“You smiled at your phone.” He laughed. “Jealous?” “Yes.” “Mehul?” Naina smiled. “Yes.” Dev shook his head. “Fair.” She stepped closer. “Do you want to kiss me?” Dev looked at her. “Yes.” “Then do not turn it into a meeting.” He laughed. Then kissed her. Naina’s hands at his shoulders. Dev’s at her waist. Longer than first. Still controlled. She stopped.

“Good.” Dev rested his forehead near hers. Not touching until she leaned in. Then. Quiet. Naina whispered: “I like that you ask.” Dev: “I like that you answer.” She smiled. “Do not make it romantic.” “Was not.” “Good.” They separated.

At 10:30, Kabir texted Rhea. Can we talk? Rhea had just left Neha’s. Arjun’s words still in her body. She replied: Parking. Same building. Kabir arrived. They sat on hood of his car. No one touched. Rhea said: “Tara?” Kabir looked at her. “Arjun?” Both laughed. Tension broke. Then returned. Kabir said:

“She affects me.” Rhea nodded. “He affects me.” Kabir looked down. “Do you want him?” Rhea thought. “I do not know.” “Do you want Tara?” Kabir answered: “I do not know.” Honest. Rhea leaned closer. “But you want me.” Kabir looked at her. “Yes.” She smiled. “Good.” He asked:

“And you?” “Yes.” Kabir’s breath changed. “Kiss?” Rhea nodded. “Yes.” They kissed beside the car. No secrecy from themselves. Still secret from everyone else. Rhea stopped. Kabir accepted. Then she said: “Do not make me your safe option because Tara is dangerous.” Kabir’s expression hardened.

“I will not.” “Good.” “And you do not make me your safe option because Arjun is married to Neha.” Rhea nodded. “Fair.” They separated. At midnight, six core friends were in three separate places. Three primary secret pairings had now kissed more than once. Three tutor dynamics were moving. Two in-law forbidden threads had names. One married couple had acknowledged outside attraction. And society friends were already inside the web.
Nothing needed a special erotic episode. The entire world had become erotically loaded
By Friday, three private rooms would test whether the heat survived without colour, music or witnesses..
